dependencies.parallel: Book 1 and Book 2 from day one
dependencies.why: Reads and checks the business numbers every engagement produces, from margins to conversion rates

dependencies.parallel: Book 3 and Book 4; the parallel-track rule starts here
dependencies.why: Equations, graphs, and logic underpin conditions in code, sizing arguments, and chart reading

dependencies.parallel: Any book from Book 6 onward; finish before Book 16
dependencies.why: The AI track gate: honest metrics, probability, and the vectors that embeddings and models are made of

dependencies.first: MA-3 (or MA-2 with MA-3 in progress)
dependencies.why: Optional specialisation: how models actually train, for engineers who must explain learning itself
A forward deployed engineer lives on customer machines; tool control is the entry fee

dependencies.parallel: MA-1, Book 3 possible after Chapter one
dependencies.why: Problem decomposition and precise steps are the daily habit behind every integration and fix

dependencies.parallel: MA-1 essentials then MA-2; no advanced maths needed
dependencies.why: Python is the programme's working language and the FDE's default automation and data tool
Turns programming into working tools: files, APIs, reports; the bread-and-butter of deployed work
Judging performance and choosing structures; also the base of technical interview practice
The professional environment: without Git and the command line, nothing later can be done properly
Customer-facing tools and dashboards start as pages; the web's mechanics repeat throughout the role
Product-grade frontend craft that makes demos land and internal tools survive real users

dependencies.parallel: Book 8; Book 10 from its early chapters
dependencies.why: APIs are the daily bread of deployed engineering; most integrations live or die here
Customer data lives in databases; SQL fluency is the fastest way to be useful in week one
Tests, review, and documentation are what make handover to customers and teams survivable
Diagnosing connectivity and process failures turns panic into a checklist during escalations
Deployment lives in the cloud; cost and access discipline prevent expensive accidents
Shipping repeatedly and safely is what separates production systems from laptop demos
Messy customer data is the opening move of nearly every engagement; pipelines make it trusted
Lets the FDE answer AI questions honestly: what is possible, what is not, and how to tell afterwards
Classical ML craft with honest evaluation; the base for models a customer can trust
Modern AI literacy: enough depth to judge, budget, and explain deep learning systems
LLM features are what customers now ask for first; this is the toolkit to build them safely
Document-heavy customer work is dominated by retrieval; grounded, cited answers win trust
Agents automate real back-office jobs when built with guardrails; restraint is the skill
The demo-to-production discipline: evaluation, monitoring, cost, and incident response for AI

dependencies.first: Book 9, Book 13 basics; Book 19 for AI chapters
dependencies.why: Trust and compliance are engineering deliverables; security failures end customer relationships

dependencies.parallel: Any time from the final phase
dependencies.why: Translates business pain into problems software can solve; the FDE's sharpest differentiator
The human craft: discovery, scoping, updates, and demos decide engagements as much as code
Design documents and integration architecture are how deployed work scales beyond one engineer
Three real capstones convert knowledge into a portfolio a hiring manager can inspect
Makes the programme's evidence legible to employers and interviews deliberate, without promising outcomes

periods.milestone: Gate A1: computer comfort, everyday maths, and precise problem-solving habits
Gate A2: first complete Python programs; algebra and logic in place
Gate B1: real-world Python tools plus algorithmic judgement
Gate B2: professional Git workflow and a published website
Gate B3: modern frontend and a tested, documented, deployed API
Gate B4: SQL fluency; the AI-track mathematics gate is open
Gate B5: hardened code with CI; network diagnosis method
Gate B6: cloud-deployed service with a full delivery pipeline
Gate C1: trusted data pipelines and honest first models
Gate C2: practitioner ML and training discipline (+optional calculus)
Gate C3: LLM features and a cited, grounded RAG assistant
Gate C4: guarded agents; security and privacy review passed
Gate C5: an operated production AI feature; business framing
Gate C6: simulated engagement delivered; design document defended
Final gate: three capstones, portfolio, and application pack complete

routes.name: Focused full-time
routes.pace: About 30 study hours per week, one period every four weeks
routes.note: The sequence table's default reading; review weeks absorbed into each period's project time

routes.name: Steady part-time
routes.pace: About 15 study hours per week, one period every eight weeks
routes.note: Same order, halved pace; keep the review queue alive between periods

routes.name: Fast-start variant
routes.pace: As chosen route, with one change
routes.note: Learners eager for code may move Book 3 alongside MA-1 in Period 1 and shift Book 2 into Period 2; the parallel-track rule allows it because Book 3 needs no advanced mathematics
